'''Considine:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Tim Wirth]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Ben Nighthorse Campbell]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Colorado}} The '''1992 United States Senate election in Colorado''' was held on November 3, 1992. Incumbent Democrat [[Tim Wirth]] decided to retire instead of seeking a second term. The open seat was won by Democratic nominee [[Ben Nighthorse Campbell]], who later switched parties in 1995 and was re-elected as a Republican in [[1998 United States Senate election in Colorado|1998]]. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== * [[Ben Nighthorse Campbell]], U.S. Representative from [[Ignacio, Colorado|Ignacio]] * [[Josie Heath]], former [[Boulder County, Colorado|Boulder County]] Commissioner and nominee for the U.S. Senate in [[1990 United States Senate election in Colorado|1990]] * [[Dick Lamm]], former [[Governor of Colorado]] ===Results=== [[File:1992 United States Senate Democratic primary in Colorado results map by county.svg|thumb|250px|Democratic primary results by county {{collapsible list | title = Campbell|{{legend|#a5b0ff|40–50%}}|{{legend|#7996e2|50–60%}}|{{legend|#6674de|60–70%}}|{{legend|#584cde|70–80%}}|{{legend|#3933e5|80–90%}}}} {{collapsible list | title = Lamm|{{legend|#ff8e65|40–50%}}|{{legend|#ff7644|50–60%}}}}|center ]] {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic Primary results{{Cite web|url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=207812|title=Our Campaigns -
